newsitem.title: MEXICO: Elektra to securitize debt on Bolsa.
newsitem.headline: Elektra to securitize debt on Bolsa.

text.p: Mexican retailer Grupo Elektra plans to securitize about 625 million pesos of its debt on the Mexican Stock Exchange to help finance its growth plans, company officials said.

"The exact amount and the return will be defined in the coming days, but we expect to issue about 625 million pesos, depending on final approval and the structure of the deal," Pablo Collado, head of investor relations, told Reuters.
"It's an important event for us, it represents a means to keep financing the great need for credit," he said.
Collado said the offer would be ready in the coming days and still needed approval by regulatory authorities. He said the debt would be issued as CPO, or ordinary, shares.
"The money will free an important part of Elektra's working capital and allow it to reduce its debt burden," he said.
He said the issue had already received a AA rating by Duff and Phelps.
Operadora de Bolsa Serfin (OBSA), a unit of Grupo Financiero Serfin will be the lead agent on the deal.
Collado said Elektra is becoming more bullish on the recovery of consumption and expects an increase of about 20 percent a year in consumer credit.

Elektra began expanding earlier this year in Central America and plans to have a total of 30-40 stores in the region this year, including a handful of new ones in the Dominican Republic, Honduras and Costa Rica.
For 1997-8, the company has capital spending plans totalling $110 million, he said.
